title: Scientific opinion on the tolerable upper intake level for vitamin D, including the derivation of a conversion factor for calcidiol monohydrate
authors: EFSA Panel on Nutrition, Novel Foods and Food Allergens (NDA), Turck D, Bohn T, Castenmiller J, de Henauw S, Hirsch-Ernst KI, et al.
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on requests from the European Commission. Preparatory systematic reviews were contracted by EFSA (OC/EFSA/NUTRI/2021/01) to the University of Helsinki with the University of Oslo.
authorConflicts: Declarations of interest of contributing experts are available on request from EFSA; not read.
result: Tolerable upper intake level 100 µg vitamin D per day for adults, including pregnant and lactating women, and for adolescents aged 11 to 17 years; 50 µg per day for children aged 1 to 10 years. Critical endpoint persistent hypercalciuria; LOAEL 250 µg per day from two randomised trials, uncertainty factor 2.5. 1 µg equals 40 IU; VITAL used 50 µg per day. Evidence tables record each included study's funding as public, private, mixed or unclear.
